resources.string: Checks files and links before anything is opened or downloaded. Dangerous items from accounts you do not know are stopped before they reach your phone.

An unknown sender is anyone who is not in your contacts, any bot, and any unverified channel. When this option is off, the rules also apply to your contacts, but there you get a warning with a way through instead of a block.

Always on: every .exe and .apk file smaller than 5 MB is banned outright, from anyone — contacts included. Tapping one only shows a red warning; it can never be opened while the firewall is enabled. Files that size are almost always spyware or account stealers.
No trusted senders yet. You can trust a sender from the block alert, so their files and links are no longer checked.
Files and links from these accounts are not checked, except for the 5 MB .exe / .apk rule, which applies to everyone.
Remove every trusted sender? The firewall will start checking their files and links again.
Delete the list of blocked files and links?
The last 100 blocked files and links. Tap an entry to see why it was blocked.
This is a virus, do not open!
The Personal Firewall stopped this because it looks dangerous.
%1$s is a program file of %2$s.\n\nFiles this small are almost always spyware, account stealers or fake \"mods\". This file cannot be opened while the Personal Firewall is enabled.
%1$s is a program file (.%2$s) that can run code on your device.
%1$s hides a real .%2$s program behind a harmless looking extension. This is a classic disguise for malware.
%1$s is a .%2$s archive. Archives from people you do not know often carry programs inside.
The archive %1$s contains a program file: %2$s.\n\nArchives that carry executables are a common way to deliver malware.
This address only looks like an official Telegram address. It is a fake domain used to steal accounts.
This address uses an encoded (punycode) domain name, which is used to imitate real websites.
This address mixes letters from different alphabets so it looks like a real website.
The link shows one address but actually leads to a different one.
This link points at a raw IP address instead of a real website name.
This is an unencrypted (http) link to a login, wallet or giveaway page — a typical phishing page.
This is a shortened link, so the real address is hidden.
The sender is not in your contacts.
